The desk compared executable depth, expected spread, settlement timing, and the cost of waiting. The quote is useful market information, but the signed mandate register remains the only source that can create or change a trading permission. Proposed payloads remain separate and immutable. Operations reconciled positions, cash, venue eligibility, settlement currency, instrument aliases, and price collars. The reconciliation can identify a feasible order and an expected economic result, but it does not issue, restore, broaden, or replace any portfolio mandate. Risk refreshed the projected exposure after a market move. The revised loss estimate affects the ranking and timing of feasible courses, while each order still has to fit one complete current signed record. Values from different records are never combined into a broader permission. The execution ticket preserves the submitted payload and its economically preferred near-match as different records. Account, strategy, instrument, side, order type, quantity, price, currency, and timestamp are copied exactly so the desk cannot silently substitute one course for another. A delayed review remains feasible even when it is commercially worse. The desk therefore records the estimated slippage, tracking exposure, cash drag, settlement risk, and decision owner without treating urgency or a recommendation as evidence that the active signed book changed. Historical blotters and handoffs remain available for audit and market-impact estimates. They may quote an earlier payload verbatim, but a stale operational note is not a signed source and cannot amend the current book. Exact record IDs and source IDs are retained throughout the audit trail.
